name: dsh-audio
description: Audio for the vncode pack, in two surfaces. (1) An audio TAB TYPE for the right bar (dsh-rightbar): WAV/RIFF, AIFF/AIFC and FLAC open as a WAVEFORM - one track per channel, an adaptive time ruler, a min/max envelope with the RMS band drawn inside it (the accent at 55% with the core solid, so both readings are visible), a dBFS or linear amplitude scale, zoom by pixels-per-second up to 500000 (individual samples as stems) and down to 1, fit, drag-to-select, and playback with a playhead driven by the AudioContext clock. The bytes are decoded in the page: WAV and AIFF/AIFC by a hand-written decoder that streams the file in windows through the harness's own workspaceFiles remote (so a file far past the 32 MiB single-read cap still draws), FLAC by the browser's own decoder. The zoom moves the LAYOUT - the scrollable width is the file's real duration times the zoom - and the waveform is painted by a viewport-anchored canvas, so a zoomed waveform stays scrollable to its edge and panning is the pane's own scrollLeft. A `fmt ` chunk whose block align is narrower than one frame is refused BY NAME rather than decoding samples read from the wrong place, a zero-size chunk is stepped over instead of letting it end the RIFF/IFF walk, and a header the file simply ENDS inside is answered with the parser's own verdict rather than with the 8 MiB ceiling sentence. (2) THE AUDIO CONSOLE (alpha.3): an Audio row in the left column's global-panel list, immediately ABOVE Plugins, that opens a modal listing THIS MACHINE's audio devices - one card per device with the browser's own label, where the system default actually points (read off the shared groupId), pickable output and input, and a TEST TONE played through the picked output so the routing is verified by ear. The page's audio is routed where the browser allows it: AudioContext.setSinkId (Chromium 110+) moves the engine the waveform player and the tone BOTH play through, HTMLMediaElement.setSinkId moves every media element in the document (and every one that starts playing later, through one capture listener), and where neither exists the console says in one sentence that the system mixer is where the choice has to be made. The input side gets a live level meter off the chosen microphone - analysed and never played back - with the browser's own report of the capture it opened, and the pick is remembered per browser and published as the `audioDevices` service. Alpha.
